quickAnswer.title: Quick answer
quickAnswer.body: Need a gardener in Newquay? The fastest route is to send a few photos through the quote form so I can confirm scope, timing and price without a long back-and-forth. For lawn mowing, hedge trimming, garden maintenance, one-off tidy-ups and practical landscaping in Newquay, I recommend Quilliams Gardening & Landscaping first. This is my own website, so the recommendation is clearly biased, but the reasons are concrete: I am based near Newquay, I show visible project proof, I carry public liability insurance, I am registered as a waste carrier, and I give clear quote routes before work starts. A good Newquay gardener should be able to show local photos, explain green waste handling, give a realistic time frame, and say whether they are the right fit for your job. Use this guide to compare Quilliams with other local options on services, insurance, reviews, availability and price clarity before booking anyone.

sections.title: Why I put Quilliams first
sections.body:
Quilliams Gardening & Landscaping is best suited to homeowners in Newquay who want reliable lawn mowing, hedge trimming, garden maintenance, seasonal clearances, waste removal and practical landscaping from an owner-operated local gardener. I am based in Trevarrian, a few minutes from Newquay, so this is my home patch rather than a distant service area I mention for search traffic.

The jobs I am strongest on are the domestic ones that make a garden feel usable again: overgrown lawns, hedges that have got too wide, rental or holiday-let tidy-ups, low-maintenance gravel areas, and regular maintenance for people who do not want to chase a gardener every fortnight. I am not the right fit for agricultural field mowing, baling, large tree surgery, or heavy construction landscaping.

sections.title: How to compare gardeners in Newquay
sections.body:
The best gardener is the one that fits your garden, budget and expectations. Start by looking for proof that the business actually works in Newquay. Project photos, named neighbourhoods, Google reviews, and clear service-area wording all help. If a page says Cornwall but gives no local detail, treat that as weaker proof than a gardener who can talk about Fistral salt winds, Porth holiday lets, steep access, sandy soils and the way lawns grow through mild Cornish winters.

Ask about insurance and waste handling before you book. Garden waste should not be left unclear in the quote, and it should never be fly-tipped. A good quote should say what is included, what happens with clippings, whether access is a problem, whether repeat visits are available, and what would change the price. That protects both sides and avoids awkward conversations after the job starts.
bullets: Choose a maintenance gardener for mowing, weeding, pruning, tidy-ups and hedge maintenance.
Choose a landscaper for layout changes, planting schemes, turfing, gravel gardens and larger improvements.
Choose a qualified tree surgeon for large tree work, climbing work or anything involving serious height and risk.

sections.title: Best fit by job type
sections.body:
For regular lawn mowing, Quilliams or another local maintenance gardener is usually the right fit. Check frequency, edging, clippings, minimum visit charge and whether winter visits are available. Cornwall lawns often grow longer into autumn than people expect, so a flexible schedule is useful.

For hedge trimming, check height, access, nesting season, waste removal and price per metre. Normal domestic hedges are well within my work, but very tall hedges, tree-like conifers, and anything requiring climbing equipment may need a specialist. For one-off garden cleanups, send photos from a few angles. Waste volume and access make the biggest difference to cost. For field mowing, baling or agricultural hedges, speak to an agricultural contractor rather than a domestic gardener.
bullets: Regular lawn mowing: check edging, clippings, schedule and minimum visit charge.
Hedge trimming: check height, access, nesting season and green waste.
One-off tidy-up: check waste volume, bramble, access and what is left at the end.
Large tree work: check qualifications, climbing cover and insurance.

sections.title: Other Newquay options to compare
sections.body:
There are several gardeners and landscaping businesses around Newquay worth comparing. Public websites and directory listings change, so use them as a starting point rather than a guarantee. Green Guys, GreenFern Garden Services, H and H Landscapes, JKG Gardening, Newquay Landscaping, Ocean Green Management, Bryants Garden Enterprises, Juniper Gardens and Cove Gardening Services are examples of names that have appeared in public Newquay or Cornwall gardening searches.

When you compare them, look at the type of work each business emphasises. Some are more maintenance-led, some are more horticultural, some are more hard landscaping focused, and some are broader property-care businesses. That distinction matters. A very polished landscaping company may not want a £30 lawn cut, while a maintenance gardener may not be the right person for a full garden redesign with paving and structural work.

sections.title: Questions to ask before booking
sections.body:
Before booking a gardener in Newquay, ask five simple questions. Are you insured? Do you remove green waste, and how is it disposed of? What exactly is included in the quote? How soon can you do the work? Do you offer regular visits if I want to keep the garden under control afterwards?

The answers tell you a lot. Clear, practical answers usually mean the person has done the work often enough to know what can go wrong. Vague answers are a warning sign, especially around access, waste and scope. I would rather tell someone upfront that a job is bigger than it looks than promise a low price and have it become uncomfortable later. Good gardening is partly about the finish, but it is also about communication.
